question.text: Under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), mutual fund AMCs are required to:

answer.text: Only verify the investor's PAN card
Report suspicious transactions only if the amount exceeds Rs. 50 lakh
Maintain records of transactions, verify client identity through KYC, and report suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU-IND)
Block all investments from NRI investors

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, and the rules and SEBI master circulars on AML/CFT, mutual fund AMCs are reporting entities and must (i) verify client identity through robust KYC, including CDD and UBO checks, (ii) maintain prescribed records of transactions and identity documents for the period stipulated by law, and (iii) report suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND), along with cash and other reportable transactions. This three-pronged obligation — KYC, record-keeping, and reporting — is the standard PMLA compliance package for financial intermediaries. The Trap: PAN verification alone is not full KYC. There is no Rs. 50 lakh threshold for STR filing — suspicious transactions are reportable regardless of amount. Blocking all NRI investments is incorrect; NRIs may invest subject to specific rules. Only the option combining KYC, record-keeping, and FIU-IND reporting captures the PMLA framework correctly. Note: The cited pages of the NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors workbook (p.71, p.187, p.196, p.200) cover PMLA-aligned KYC, cash-investment limits, client due diligence, UBO verification, and KYC record-registry mechanics, but the specific duties to maintain transaction records and report suspicious transactions to FIU-IND were not found in those pages. The framing above is general PMLA/AML regulatory knowledge applicable to mutual fund AMCs.
